findings.title: Missing data processing agreement and GDPR flow-down
findings.impact: AtliQ conflicts its data protection obligations under the client contract by engaging an offshore subcontractor to process personal data without compliant sub-processor terms.

citations.docTitle: Kriti Data Labs subcontractor agreement (AtliQ draft)
citations.quote: Source data comprises vibration, temperature and pressure sensor streams from End Client customer plants, together with maintenance work orders and technician logs (including technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes

To the extent Supplier processes personal data on behalf of Client, the Parties shall conclude the Data Processing Agreement pursuant to Art. 28 GDPR attached as **Annex 3**, which forms an integral part of this Agreement

findings.standard: DPA (EU) or BAA (US health) signed before any personal/regulated data moves, with a sub-DPA / sub-BAA for every party that touches the data (incl. AtliQ's own Pune entity); engagement-specific scope; offshore access only as the agreement allows.
findings.counterPosition: Execute a back-to-back DPA and EU SCCs (sub-processor terms) with Vendor before any personal data is accessed or processed.
